items.question: A rectangular wooden block with a height of 8 cm rests on a table. The base of the block in contact with the table has a length of 15 cm and a width of 10 cm. The block exerts a force of 45 N on the table. What is the pressure exerted by the block on the table in N/cm²?
items.explanation: First, calculate the area of the base in contact with the table. Area = length × width = 15 cm × 10 cm = 150 cm². The height of 8 cm is not needed for this calculation (irrelevant datum). Pressure = Force ÷ Area = 45 N ÷ 150 cm² = 0.3 N/cm². Option B (3 N/cm²) is a trap for students who might use only one dimension (45 ÷ 15). Option C is a magnitude error. Option D is for students who invert the calculation.

items.question: A hydraulic system has a circular piston with a radius of 4 cm. The piston experiences a total force of 240 N. Using π = 3, calculate the pressure exerted on the piston in Pa. (Note: 1 N/cm² = 10 000 Pa)
items.explanation: First, calculate the area of the circular piston. Area = π × r² = 3 × 4² = 3 × 16 = 48 cm². Pressure in N/cm² = Force ÷ Area = 240 N ÷ 48 cm² = 5 N/cm². Convert to Pa using the conversion factor: 1 N/cm² = 10 000 Pa, so 5 N/cm² = 5 × 10 000 = 50 000 Pa. Option A (5 000 Pa) is a trap for students who forget to multiply by 10 000 or use 1 000 incorrectly. Option C is for students who multiply by 100 000 instead. Option D is for students who square the conversion factor.

items.question: A cube with an edge length of 6 cm and a mass of 540 g rests on one of its faces on a flat surface. The cube exerts a pressure of 2.5 N/cm² on the surface. What is the force exerted by the cube on the surface?
items.explanation: The cube rests on one square face. Area of one face = edge × edge = 6 cm × 6 cm = 36 cm². Using the formula Pressure = Force ÷ Area, we rearrange to get Force = Pressure × Area = 2.5 N/cm² × 36 cm² = 90 N. The mass of 540 g is an irrelevant datum in this problem. Option A (15 N) is a trap for students who use only one edge length (2.5 × 6). Option C is for students who calculate 2.5 × 90. Option D matches the mass value, trapping students who confuse mass with force.

items.question: A machine part initially exerts a pressure of 8 N/cm² over a contact area of 25 cm². The contact area is then reduced to 10 cm² while the force remains constant. What is the new pressure exerted by the machine part?
items.explanation: First, calculate the constant force. Force = Pressure × Area = 8 N/cm² × 25 cm² = 200 N. When the area changes to 10 cm², the new pressure = Force ÷ New Area = 200 N ÷ 10 cm² = 20 N/cm². Alternatively, using ratio: when area decreases from 25 cm² to 10 cm² (ratio 25:10 = 5:2), pressure increases in inverse ratio from 8 N/cm² by factor 25/10 = 2.5, giving 8 × 2.5 = 20 N/cm². Option A (3.2 N/cm²) is a trap for students who incorrectly apply direct proportion (8 × 10/25). Option B is for students who calculate 25/10 × 8 ÷ 2. Option D is for students who multiply 8 × 25/10 × 2.

items.question: A storage container with a rectangular base of length 20 cm and width 15 cm exerts a pressure of 1.2 N/cm² on the ground. Calculate the total force exerted by the container on the ground, then express this force in Pascals if it were distributed over an area of 1 cm². (Note: 1 N/cm² = 10 000 Pa)
items.explanation: First, calculate the area of the rectangular base. Area = length × width = 20 cm × 15 cm = 300 cm². Force = Pressure × Area = 1.2 N/cm² × 300 cm² = 360 N. The question asks for this force expressed in Pascals if distributed over 1 cm². Pressure = 360 N ÷ 1 cm² = 360 N/cm². Converting to Pa: 1 N/cm² = 10 000 Pa, so 360 N/cm² = 360 × 10 000 Pa. However, we need to reconsider: the original pressure is 1.2 N/cm². Converting this to Pa: 1.2 N/cm² = 1.2 × 10 000 = 12 000 Pa. This is the pressure value in Pa, which equals force per 1 cm² in Pa. Option A (360 Pa) traps students who don't convert properly. Option B is for students who use 1 000 as conversion. Option D is for students who multiply 360 × 1 000.

items.question: A rectangular wooden block with a height of 8 cm rests on a table. The base in contact with the table has dimensions 15 cm by 10 cm. If the block exerts a force of 45 N on the table, what is the pressure exerted on the table in Pa?
items.explanation: First, calculate the contact area: Area = 15 cm × 10 cm = 150 cm². Convert to m²: 150 cm² ÷ 10000 = 0.015 m² (since 1 m² = 10000 cm²). Pressure = Force ÷ Area = 45 N ÷ 0.015 m² = 3000 Pa. Wait, let me recalculate: 45 ÷ 0.015 = 45 ÷ (15/1000) = 45 × (1000/15) = 45000/15 = 3000 Pa. However, checking again: 150 cm² = 150/10000 m² = 0.015 m². Pressure = 45/0.015 = 3000 Pa. The height of 8 cm is irrelevant to this calculation. Option B (3000 Pa) would be if students correctly converted. Let me recalculate the entire problem: Area = 150 cm², converting: 150/10000 = 0.015 m². P = 45/0.015 = 3000 Pa. So answer should be B, not A. Regenerating...

items.question: A cube exerts a pressure of 2400 Pa when resting on surface A, which has an area of 0.008 m². The cube is then turned to rest on surface B, which has an area of 60 cm². What is the new pressure exerted on surface B in Pa?
items.real_world_context: Rotating objects to change contact area
items.explanation: First, find the force: Force = Pressure × Area = 2400 Pa × 0.008 m² = 19.2 N. The force remains constant when the cube is turned. Convert area B to m²: 60 cm² ÷ 10000 = 0.006 m² (since 1 m² = 10000 cm²). New pressure = Force ÷ Area B = 19.2 N ÷ 0.006 m² = 3200 Pa. Option D (1920 Pa) is a trap for students who incorrectly multiply 2400 × 0.008 ÷ 0.01 using wrong conversion.

items.question: A metal cylinder with a circular base of radius 4 cm exerts a pressure of 1.5 N/cm² on a platform. What is the force exerted by the cylinder in N?
items.explanation: First, calculate the area of the circular base: Area = π × r² = 3.14 × 4² = 3.14 × 16 = 50.24 cm². Force = Pressure × Area = 1.5 N/cm² × 50.24 cm² = 75.36 N. Option B (18.84 N) is a trap for students who incorrectly calculate area using 2πr instead of πr².

givens.name: Ratio of area X to area Y

items.question: A hydraulic system has two pistons X and Y. The ratio of the area of piston X to piston Y is 3:5. If piston Y has an area of 0.02 m² and a total force of 240 N is applied to piston X, what is the pressure exerted on piston X in Pa?
items.explanation: From the ratio 3:5, if area Y = 0.02 m² represents 5 parts, then 1 part = 0.02 ÷ 5 = 0.004 m². Area X = 3 parts = 3 × 0.004 = 0.012 m². Pressure on X = Force ÷ Area X = 240 N ÷ 0.012 m² = 20000 Pa. Option B (12000 Pa) is a trap for students who incorrectly use area Y instead of area X in the final calculation.

items.question: A square plate with side length 25 cm exerts a pressure of 8000 Pa on a surface. The plate is being cut at a rate of 5 cm per minute from each side. After 3 minutes, what is the new pressure exerted by the plate in Pa, assuming the force remains constant?
items.explanation: Initial area = 25 cm × 25 cm = 625 cm² = 0.0625 m² (since 1 m² = 10000 cm²). Initial force = 8000 Pa × 0.0625 m² = 500 N. After 3 minutes, total decrease = 5 cm/min × 3 min = 15 cm. New side length = 25 - 15 = 10 cm. New area = 10 cm × 10 cm = 100 cm² = 0.01 m². New pressure = 500 N ÷
